note: Ready-made design systems as plain values. QuorX writes DESIGN.md and tokens.css from these (server/design.js). The hand-written starters are the folders beside this file.

systems.name: Paperwhite
systems.description: Quiet, airy and almost colourless, with one ink-blue accent. For personal sites, docs, notes apps and anything where the words matter most.
systems.look: A sheet of good paper: warm white ground, near-black ink, wide margins and very little decoration. One ink-blue accent marks links and the main action. Everything else is spacing and type.
dos: leave generous white space around every block
keep pages to one column for reading
donts: add icons, gradients or coloured panels for decoration

systems.name: Concrete
systems.description: Raw and loud: thick black borders, hard offset shadows, square corners and a hazard-yellow accent. For portfolios, zines, indie products and launches that want to be noticed.
systems.look: Unpolished on purpose. Thick 3px black borders, square corners, hard shadows with no blur, a heavy grotesque in capitals for headlines and a mono for labels. Yellow is the one shout.
dos: let blocks collide and overlap a little
use the mono for labels, prices and dates

systems.name: Frost
systems.description: Frosted glass panels floating over a deep blue-violet night, with soft light and an ice-cyan accent. For product launches, music, weather and app landing pages.
systems.look: Translucent cards over a dark, softly lit background. Panels use --surface at 70% opacity with backdrop-filter: blur(18px) and a 1px light border at 12%. Keep text on solid enough surfaces to read easily.
dos: put one or two large blurred colour blobs behind the content
blur panels with backdrop-filter
donts: stack glass on glass more than once
put long body text on very transparent panels

systems.name: Broadsheet
systems.description: A magazine page: high-contrast serif headlines, narrow columns, rules between sections and a deep red accent. For blogs, publications, long reads and newsletters.
systems.look: Classic editorial typography. A sharp display serif for headlines, a book serif for reading, thin rules between sections, small caps labels and a deep red for kickers and links.
dos: set reading text at 65 characters a line
use thin rules instead of boxes

systems.name: Confetti
systems.description: Bright, bouncy and rounded, with a bubbly headline face and a candy palette. For games, kids' apps, parties, clubs and friendly consumer products.
systems.look: Cheerful and soft: big rounded corners, chunky headlines, playful colour on a cream ground. One magenta accent for actions, with sunny yellow and mint as supporting colours in illustrations.
dos: use simple shapes (circles, squiggles) as decoration
keep buttons big and round
donts: make every element a different colour

systems.name: Boardroom
systems.description: Clean, confident SaaS look: crisp sans, cool greys, a trustworthy blue and tidy cards. For B2B products, company sites, pricing pages and admin tools.
systems.look: Professional without being dull. Plenty of structure: a clear grid, cards with soft shadows, a dependable blue for actions and calm cool greys for everything else.
dos: show real product screenshots
keep one primary action per section

systems.name: Neon Grid
systems.description: Cyberpunk night: near-black ground, glowing magenta and cyan, mono labels and a faint grid. For games, hackathons, crypto-free tech events and music.
systems.look: Electric and dark. A black-violet ground with a faint 40px grid, mono labels in capitals, and two neon colours that glow (text-shadow 0 0 12px at 60%). Magenta is the action; cyan is information.
dos: let the neon glow only on headings and the main action
use thin 1px borders in --line
donts: use more than two neon colours

systems.name: Arcade 84
systems.description: Eighties arcade: pixel headlines, sunset orange and hot pink on deep purple, chunky borders. For games, retro shops, events and fun side projects.
systems.look: A cabinet at night. A pixel font for headlines only (short words), a clear sans for everything else, sunset orange and hot pink on a deep purple, and chunky square borders.
dos: keep pixel text to a few words
use a horizon-line or sun graphic once
donts: set paragraphs in the pixel font

systems.name: Material Sky
systems.description: Familiar app look: tonal surfaces, rounded containers, a friendly blue and clear elevation. For Android-style apps, dashboards, forms and productivity tools.
systems.look: Calm, systematic and familiar. Tonal surfaces instead of borders, pill-shaped buttons, rounded containers, and elevation by soft shadow. Blue is primary; teal is secondary.
dos: make buttons pill-shaped and 40px tall
group content in tonal containers

systems.name: Zurich
systems.description: International Typographic Style: a strict 12-column grid, big grotesque headlines, flush-left text and one red. For agencies, museums, posters and architecture.
systems.look: Rational and bold. Everything aligns to a 12-column grid, text is flush left, headlines are huge and tight, and red is used like a printed spot colour. White space does the work.
dos: align every edge to the grid
use size contrast instead of colour

systems.name: Terracotta
systems.description: Warm and earthy: clay, sand and olive tones, a soft serif and gentle curves. For cafés, restaurants, wellness, crafts and sustainable brands.
systems.look: Sun-warmed and natural. Sand grounds, clay-red actions, olive accents, a soft serif for headlines and rounded, organic shapes. Photos of real materials suit it well.
dos: use organic blob shapes behind photos
write in a warm, human voice
donts: use pure black or pure white

systems.name: Maison
systems.description: Quiet luxury: a refined high-contrast serif, ivory and charcoal, thin gold lines and lots of space. For fashion, hotels, jewellery, real estate and fine dining.
systems.look: Expensive restraint. Ivory grounds, charcoal text, a light, elegant serif for headlines (often in capitals with wide spacing), hairline gold rules and generous margins. Nothing shouts.
dos: use large photography with lots of space around it
letter-space small capital labels

systems.name: Marshmallow
systems.description: Soft pastels: lilac, peach and mint on a cloud-white ground, rounded and gentle. For lifestyle apps, journaling, baby products, beauty and gentle wellbeing tools.
systems.look: Light and gentle. Pastel surfaces (lilac, peach, mint) as card fills, deep plum text for readability, large rounded corners and soft shadows. The accent is a deeper violet-plum so buttons stay readable.
dos: fill cards with soft pastel tints
use simple line icons

systems.name: Phosphor
systems.description: A green-screen terminal: monospace everything, phosphor green on black, square boxes drawn with lines. For developer tools, CLIs, hacker events and retro-tech pages.
systems.look: An old monitor. Monospace for every piece of text, phosphor green on black, amber for warnings, boxes drawn with 1px lines and a blinking block cursor as the one flourish.
dos: prefix prompts with > or $
use ASCII-style dividers

systems.name: Pulse
systems.description: Calm and reassuring care look: soft teal, clean white, rounded friendly sans and plenty of space. For clinics, healthcare, insurance and support services.
systems.look: Clean and caring. White and pale-teal grounds, a deep teal for actions, a friendly rounded sans, clear forms with large hit areas and plain-language headings.
dos: make buttons and inputs at least 44px tall
say what happens next in plain words
donts: use red for anything but errors

systems.name: Vault
systems.description: Precise fintech look: deep navy, mint for gains and coral for losses, tabular mono numbers. For banking, trading-free finance dashboards, budgets and invoices.
systems.look: Serious and exact. Deep navy text on near-white, mint and coral reserved for up and down, tabular mono numbers right-aligned, tight data tables and clear hierarchy in cards.
dos: right-align numbers in the mono
show gains and losses with a sign and a word, not only colour
donts: use green and red as the brand colours

systems.name: Level Up
systems.description: Gaming energy: dark slate, electric lime and violet, angled shapes and bold condensed headlines. For game studios, esports, streamers and gaming communities.
systems.look: Fast and bold. Dark slate grounds, electric lime for actions, violet for highlights, bold condensed capitals, and cut corners (clip-path) on buttons and cards.
dos: cut one corner of buttons and cards at 45°
use big key art behind the hero

systems.name: Sketchbook
systems.description: Handmade and personal: a handwritten headline face, notebook paper, marker-yellow highlights and wobbly lines. For personal blogs, workshops, teachers and craft makers.
systems.look: A page from a notebook. Cream paper with faint ruled lines, handwritten headlines, marker-yellow highlights behind key words, a blue-ink accent and slightly irregular hand-drawn borders.
dos: highlight a key word with a yellow marker stripe
use doodle-style SVG arrows
donts: set body text in the handwritten font

systems.name: Fjord
systems.description: Nordic calm: cool greys, birch white, a muted spruce green and clean geometric type. For furniture, architecture, design studios and thoughtful products.
systems.look: Scandinavian simplicity. Cool, light greys, a muted spruce green accent, clean geometric sans, honest materials in photos and a lot of quiet space.
dos: use natural-light photography
keep headlines short and quiet

systems.name: Clear View
systems.description: High-contrast and easy to read for everyone: big type, strong focus rings, underlined links and AAA contrast. For public services, forms, education and older audiences.
systems.look: Readability first. Large body text (18px), very high contrast, links always underlined, thick yellow-and-black focus rings, generous hit areas and one strong blue for actions.
dos: underline every link
show a 3px focus ring with an outline offset

systems.name: Gazette
systems.description: An old newspaper front page: dense columns, a blackletter-feel serif masthead, hairline rules and sepia paper. For local news, history projects, archives and newsletters.
systems.look: Newsprint. Sepia paper, black ink, dense multi-column layout, hairline and double rules, a bold serif masthead, small caps datelines and no colour except a faded red for breaking items.
dos: use three or four text columns on wide screens
use double rules under the masthead
